articles.title: A España se le sigue resistiendo el oro mundial en hockey
articles.standfirst: Jugó una gran final pero pagó cara su falta de acierto ante una Alemania que aprovechó un desafortunado rebote para revalidar la corona. Enorme campeonato de los de Max Caldas
articles.summary: Jugó una gran final pero pagó cara su falta de acierto ante una Alemania que aprovechó un desafortunado rebote para revalidar la corona. Enorme campeonato de los de Max Caldas
articles.body: "Cabeza y corazón" arengaba Marc Miralles, capitán de la selección española de hockey, en el círculo previo a la final del Mundial de hockey. Y los 'Redsticks' pusieron ambos en el Belfius Hockey Arena de Wavre (Bélgica), pero les faltó el gol. A la tercera no fue la vencida y a España se le volvió a escapar el oro mundial. La primera vez fue en Barcelona 1971 por un penalti córner, la segunda en Utrecht 1998 por un gol de oro en la prórroga y hoy, pese a que los de Max Caldas hicieron un gran partido ante Alemania, un gol de Michel Strurhoff en el tercer cuarto dejó a los 'Redsticks' a las puertas de la historia. La plata, que es la cuarta medalla mundial española para la selección masculina, devuelve a los ‘Redsticks’ al podio en una Copa del Mundo 20 años después de aquel bronce en 2006 en Mönchengladbach (Alemania), pero sobre todo deja muy buenas sensaciones a dos años de Los Ángeles 2028. Se marcha de Wavre con la cabeza muy alta y con la sensación de que mereció más. Porque España se plantó en la final habiendo dejado por el camino a favoritos como el campeón olímpico Países Bajos o Bélgica, líder del ranking mundial. Y aunque Caldas no quiere hablar de milagro, sólo comparar el número de licencias nos da una idea de la dimensión de la plata. En España hay 16.988 frente a las 220.000 fichas de los neerlandeses o a las 85.000 de los germanos, tetracampeones mundiales, plata olímpica en París 2024 y campeones de Europa. Este domingo, los 'Redsticks' saltaron al campo con la medalla asegurada en el bolsillo -faltaba por saber el color- para volver a disputar una final mundialista 28 años después. El equipo estaba convencido de que podían hacerlo porque España ya había batido a su rival en la segunda fase de este mismo campeonato. El primer cuarto de la final comenzó con dominio germano. La primera ocasión llegó con una penetración alemana que forzó el primer penalti-córner al minuto y medio. Tiro centrado de Benedikt Schwarzhaupt que sacó Luis Calzado evitando el primero. España empezó a combinar bien y en el minuto 9, Marc Reyné sacó petróleo desde la línea de fondo cuando se había quedado sin salida de la bola y provocó un penalti córner. Fue bien bloqueado por los alemanes, que montaron un contragolpe peligroso pero, por suerte, el disparo acabó fuera de los tres palos que defiende Calzado. Después de un primer cuarto de tanteo y sin goles, España comenzó el segundo mostrándose muy sólida en la presión y en la defensa de medio campo, pero le faltaba convertir las recuperaciones en ataques peligrosos. Sí lo logró en dos ocasiones que fueron desbaratadas por Danneberg. La primera a un gran tiro de Borja Lacalle y la segunda, de ‘Chefo’ Basterra, que se marcha del Mundial con siete goles, pero cuya acción fue anulada al darle por el lado curvo del stick. Alemania respondió al empuje español, pero los goles no llegaron por ninguno de los dos bandos y ambos equipos se fueron al descanso con empate a cero. Los 'RedSticks' se iban al vestuario dejando muy buenas sensaciones, sólo faltaba el gol. Cuatro ocasiones por su parte, dos por la alemana y con una posesión prácticamente al 50% para ambos. Todo por decidir. Tras el descanso, llegaron los mejores minutos de España, que dominaba el partido entrando por ambas bandas. La primera ocasión de gol llegó nada más empezar el tercer cuarto. La cruzó Cunill, la bola pasó entre dos jugadores alemanes y le llegó a Basterra, que no la esperaba y no acertó a rematar. Los de Max Caldas generaban más peligro, pero se les seguía resistiendo el gol. Una gran contra de Pol Cabré provocó el penalti-córner y el disparo de Marc Miralles casi se cantó como gol, pero la bola salió rozando el palo izquierdo. En los mejores momentos españoles llegó el gol de Alemania. Quedaba menos de un minuto y medio para acabar el tercer cuarto y Michel Struthoff recogió una bola suelta en el área pequeña, que había rebotado accidentalmente en el pie de Pepe Cunill, y solo ante Calzado le batió a placer (min.44). España reaccionó con un doble penalti-córner que no fue capaz de convertir. Quedaban 15 minutos por delante para remontar, como ya hicieron ante Alemania en la segunda fase o Bélgica, y tratar de coser su primera estrella en la camiseta. En el primer minuto del último cuarto, Calzado salvó el segundo a disparo de Groose dando una auténtica lección de reflejos. España siguió con su masterclass de hockey, combinando, presionando, pero siempre se encontró con Danneberg. A falta de a 3:46 para el desenlace, Caldas sacó al portero español del campo y dio entrada a un jugador de campo para tratar de aprovechar la superioridad. España presionaba como si no hubiera un mañana, quería hacer historia pero esta vez no hubo épica. "Yo me quedo con que hemos jugado un torneo increíble. Hemos hecho un buen partido defensivo ante Alemania, pero nos ha faltado un poco más cara a gol", reconoció Calzado, nombrado mejor portero del Mundial. "Somos un equipo muy joven que está aprendiendo a jugar este tipo de partidos. Hemos demostrado que somos un equipo muy sólido. Quedan dos años para Los Ángeles y paso a paso estaremos más cerca de conseguir las medallas allí", añadió. "Como equipo creo que merecíamos un poco más. Hemos jugado un muy buen hockey pero así es el deporte. Somos un equipo con mucha ambición y con mucho trabajo. Podemos dar muchas alegrías aún", avisó Marc Miralles.

articles.title: Quién es quién en los subcampeones del mundo de hockey
articles.standfirst: La media de edad está en torno a los 27 años, perfil universitario y el 60 por ciento juegan fuera
articles.summary: La media de edad está en torno a los 27 años, perfil universitario y el 60 por ciento juegan fuera
articles.body: Una veintena de chicos, de una media de edad de 27 años, surgidos en su mayoría de Barcelona, aunque también de Madrid, y con numerosos perfiles en Linkedin, señal inequívoca de que además de jugar al hockey son universitarios, se quedaron a las puertas de la conquista del mundo. Así son los subcampeones del planeta hockey, que tienen seis veces menos licencias que su oponente alemán en la final: 15.000 frente a 90.000, sumando todas las categorías. Con la ayuda de Nacho Usoz, comentarista de TVE y una figura de referencia en el hockey español, así es el grupo que ha igualado la cota más alta masculina en la historia. Portero. Juega en el Kampong de Países Bajos el campeón de la última Euroliga. Nieto de un medallista olímpico de Roma 60. Su participación fue clave para meter a España en la final con una soberbia actuación ante Paises Bajos. Es muy bueno en el uno contra uno. En el gol no pudo hacer nada. Portero. Juega en el Club de Campo. Otro que sabe lo que es ser olímpico. Es muy fiable bajo los palos y tiene una gran experiencia. Un fijo desde hace años. Centrocampista. Milita en el Real Club de Polo, tras haber vivido la experiencia de la Liga de Países Bajos. Es de los jugadores por encima de la centena de internacionalidades. Es el capitán y el organizador. La primera referencia en los penaltis córner, un apartado en el que España necesita crecer en efectividad para dominar el planeta. Defensa. Juega en el RC Polo. Ingeniero industrial. Hizo el TFG sobre el análisis de tecnologías disruptivas para la optimización del rendimiento y la gestión en el hockey profesional. Se anticipa bien, es un defensa en progresión. Centrocampista. Juega en el Canberra Chill australiano. Nieto de pionero de los 60 (Jaume Amat) y sobrino de una leyenda como Pol Amat. Se ha contagiado del rugby australiano, muy directo, rápido y físico. Sabe romper muy bien la primera presión y es clave en la conducción vertical. Defensa. Del Atlétic Terrassa. Otro de los contrastados atrás. Es polivalente, también se emplea en el centro del campo. Un gran jugador cuando hay que subir por banda. Ejercita la presión como pocos. Defensa también del Atlétic Terrassa. Otro especialista en los penaltis córner. Autor de uno de los goles ante Países Bajos. Un jugador muy hábil en los Drag-flick, las bolas por alto. Delantero. Juega en el Royal Leopold belga. Dos Juegos Olímpicos en su palmarés. Ha marcado siete goles en el Mundial, dos de ellos en la fase anterior ante Alemania y tres en la semifinal ante Países Bajos. Es un ariete de época. Delantero. Juega en el HC Rotterdam holandés. Campeón olímpico en 2016... con Argentina. Cambió de país -tenía también la nacionalidad española- por discrepancias con el cuerpo técnico. Es un jugador muy fiable. Pone la experiencia, la pausa y el último pase. Centrocampista del Club de Campo. Su tio-abuelo Jorge Solaun disputó los Juegos de Tokio 64 y México 68. Su aportación en ataque se centra en darle mucha movilidad a la delantera. Irrumpe bien desde la segunda línea. Defensa del Royal Leopold de Bélgica. Otro de los que ya contabiliza dos Juegos Olímpicos. Tiene un gran sentido de la anticipación y con más de 160 internacionalidades, el santanderino pone la experiencia en la zaga. Centrocampista. Milita en el Junior FC, de Sant Cugat. Tiene sólo 21 años, pero la experiencia de un veterano. Posee una buena técnica y gran llegada. Defensa del HC Rotterdam. Es uno de los grandes en la zaga española. Maneja bien el timing del partido, es brillante en las coberturas y maneja muy bien la salida de la bola bajo presión. Centrocampista/delantero del Oranje Rood de Países Bajos. El complemento ideal a Basterra. Un jugador con una gran habilidad para el desmarque, de gran habilidad y gran agresividad en el área. Centrocampista del Oranje Rood. Ha estudiado contabilidad financiera. Aporta ritmo, presión y equilibrio entre líneas. Tiene un gran sentido de la orientación del juego. Delantero del Oranje Rood. Es un jugador de fantasía, con un gran manejo del stick para robar arriba. Su imaginación es un plus en la selección. Tiene talento y buena llegada al área. Defensa del Den Bosch de Países Bajos. Forjado en la cantera del Atlétic Terrassa. Es un jugador muy disciplinado, que trabaja por dentro y con un gran sentido de control del ritmo. Delantero del Braxgata belga. Ataca muy bien el segundo palo y aparece en momentos decisivos del juego. Estuvo brillante en los Juegos Olímpicos de París. Defensa del Royal Uccle belga. Su padre fue medallista en los Juegos Olímpicos de Atlanta 1996. Tiene un gran físico y una gran capacidad para la presión y sostener transiciones. Delantero del RC Polo. Es un jugador con un gran presente (16 goles en la Pro League) y un futuro muy interesante. Tras pasar por el Tenis de Santander, como Alonso, recaló en el club barcelonés la temporada pasada.

articles.title: Titans release Cordell Volson, former Bengals offensive lineman
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans are releasing former Cincinnati Bengals offensive lineman Cordell Volson.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans are releasing former Cincinnati Bengals offensive lineman Cordell Volson, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Volson was injured during training camp in 2025 and missed the entire season. He signed with the Titans in March after becoming a free agent after the season.

Volson, who turned 28 in July, didn't miss a game during his first three seasons with the Bengals, starting 48 of the 50 games in which he played. He also played in three playoff games during the 2022 postseason.

articles.title: Report: Browns moving on from preseason star wide receiver
articles.summary: Reports indicate the Browns are moving on from their preseason star Luke Floriea.
articles.body:
Roster cutdown day is never a fun day to cover the game of football. You see countless dreams and hard work fall apart, but amid all that chaos and destruction, you also see dreams come true.

In the middle of all the chaos, sadly, one fan favorite and local player will not continue his Cinderella run on the Browns .

UDFA wide receiver Floriea is being waived after a strong preseason stretch for the Browns. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler first reported the news.

The former Kent State Golden Flash was hoping to make the 53-man roster after being with the team's practice squad since last season. He dominated the preseason with six passes caught for 95 yards and an impressive three touchdowns, including one that was overturned after review.

He had a knack for getting open and finding the endzone, now Browns fans have to wait and see if he will make it back to them once again.

articles.title: Jaguars UDFA reportedly making initial 53-man roster
articles.summary: One of the Jaguars' UDFAs is reportedly making the team's initial 53-man roster after a strong preseason.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars UDFA edge rusher Bryan Thomas Jr. is reportedly making the team's initial 53-man roster, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.

Thomas Jr. had been a standout performer during the preseason, and he capped off his impressive summer with a dominant outing in the team's preseason finale.

Against Tampa Bay, Thomas logged five pressures, according to Pro Football Focus, and he was in on three sacks.

In total over the three preseason games, Thomas Jr. logged eight pressures and four sacks. Head coach Liam Coen also noted his play against the run.

"His play style is the right way," Coen said after the final preseason game. "It fits a lot of the things that we preach and that we're about as a team. When you have a gift of rushing the passer, man, it's something that you can't ignore. I thought he did some nice things against the run as well tonight. I thought the defense as a whole, obviously with the shutout, was huge, being led by Bryan. He's making it really difficult, which is a good thing. It's just what we're hunting up. He's had that skill set. That was something we really appreciated about his game. He's just continued to do it on this stage."

In a crowded defensive end room, Thomas Jr. faced an uphill battle when it came to making the final roster, but his steady production and regular flashes helped him stand out.

Fellow defensive ends Danny Striggow and BJ Green each made the Jaguars ' 53-man roster last year as UDFAs.

articles.title: Bears expected to waive top undrafted free agent offensive lineman
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears are expected to part ways with undrafted free agent guard Caden Barnett amid roster cuts.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears are expected to waive undrafted free agent offensive lineman Caden Barnett, according to Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs .

Barnett, who played both guard and tackle at Wyoming, worked exclusively at right guard with Chicago this summer, and he was contending with fellow guards Jordan McFadden and Luke Newman, who are both expected to earn a roster spot.

Biggs noted that Barnett, who received $277,500 guaranteed when he initially signed, is strongly expected to re-sign to the practice squad.

articles.title: Denver Broncos have waived cornerback Brent Austin
articles.summary: According to Mike Klis of 9News, the Denver Broncos have waived cornerback Brent Austin.
articles.body:
According to Mike Klis of 9News, the Denver Broncos have waived cornerback Brent Austin today.

Austin was an undrafted rookie free agent cornerback who started at James Madison before transferring to USF. He ended up finishing his college career with two seasons at Cal. That season he posted forty-two tackles and thirteen pass deflections. He is a guy we viewed as a developmental candidate on the practice squad as rookie:

All things considered, it seems most realistic that Austin will have a good shot at earning a spot on the practice squad for continued development. You can never have enough quality cover players, and Austin's collegiate tape and resume show a promising player who has the ability to contribute as a reserve player in the future.

He had a great training camp as an undrafted rookie, but the cornerback position is a stacked one in Denver. I would look for him to be a priority addition to the practice squad based on what little we've gotten from camp reports.

articles.title: Report: Saints made their decision about this year's starting kicker
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints have been all over the place with kickers since trading Wil Lutz, and now, 2026 will be opened by a different starter again.
articles.body:
Over the course of the New Orleans Saints ' 58 seasons of existence, they have had 37 different kickers attempt at least one kick during a regular-season game. One of the most notable during that time frame was Wil Lutz, holding down the fort for seven seasons before being traded to the Denver Broncos .

Since then, the Saints have utilized two options, Blake Grupe and Charlie Smyth, who both had their bright spots and low moments. Now, Smyth was let go before the NFL roster cuts deadline ( but could return on the practice squad ). For 2026, they will rely on another option, though, as recently signed two-time All-Pro Daniel Carlson will take the reins to open the season, as was reported by Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football .

Carlson was picked up before the third preseason game for New Orleans, and in that third matchup, he had three kicking attempts, making two field goals and an extra point, including a 53-yard bomb that likely won him the job. After spotty performances from Smyth and Tanner Brown this summer, Carlson will step in and earn a starting job for his ninth consecutive season.

articles.title: The Seattle Seahawks 2026 roster cuts tracker
articles.summary: Before taking to the field to defend their Lombardi Trophy, the Seahawks will make dozens of roster decisions in the coming days.
articles.body:
The NFL offseason is all but officially over for the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, with the regular season set to kick off on Wednesday, September 9.

To start the season off with a bang, the Hawks will be looking to open the 2026 campaign the same way they closed out 2025, and that is by thumping the New England Patriots. The Seahawks are currently 3.5 point favorites over the Pats at FanDuel Sportsbook , and coming away victorious would allow Mike Macdonald to claim a third win over the Pats in three seasons as head coach in Seattle.

Before getting to the game and on-field action, though, Seahawks general manager John Schneider will need to trim the roster from 91 players down to 53, which means no shortage of roster transactions in the coming days as the team makes the moves necessary to pare the roster down to the allowed limit.

Rather than simply waiving or releasing 38 players, there will almost certainly be players moved to injured reserve or traded away as Schneider works to build the fringes of the roster as competitively as possible. Regardless of the combination of moves Seattle makes, Field Gulls will work to keep readers up to date on all the rumored and reported transactions between now and 6 PM New York time on Sunday, August 30.

articles.title: Falcons waive two promising undrafted free agents
articles.summary: Falcons waive undrafted WR Vinny Anthony, C James Brockermeyer ahead of deadline
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons waived undrafted wide receiver Vinny Anthony II and offensive lineman James Brockermeyer ahead of the NFL's 53-man roster deadline on Sunday evening. Both Anthony and Brockermeyer were training camp standouts.

Anthony made noise as a kick returner. He averaged 30 yards per kickoff return in the preseason opener against the Denver Broncos, and broke loose for a 52-yard return in Friday's preseason finale against the Miami Dolphins . According to ESPN's Marc Raimondi, Anthony will likely sign with the team's practice squad once cuts are complete.

Brockermeyer was another one of the Falcons' priority UDFA signings after the draft. The former Miami Huricanes standout showed some promise in camp as well. Offensive line coach Bill Callahan praised Brockermeyer after filling in for starting center Ryan Neuzil in camp.

"I'm really proud of the job he did today," Callahan said of Brockermeyer . "He had to step up and step in and take over the controls. He did a great job. He was like the air traffic controller today, so he landed all the planes safely, which was great."

The Falcons' roster has been trimmed down to 71 players with less than three hours until the 53-man deadline at 6 p.m. ET. Check out the full list of cuts and updated roster as it currently stands below.

articles.title: OU football vs UTEP TV channel, odds, scouting report for Sooners-Miners
articles.summary: Here's a look at what you need to know ahead of OU football's season-opener against UTEP on Friday.
articles.body:
NORMAN — Oklahoma 's season opens this week.

The Sooners host UTEP at 7 p.m. Friday at Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium.

Here's a look at what you need to know about the game:

OU football QB John Mateer, Sooners practice in 2026 preseason, see top photos

Where: Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium

Best player: Transfer wide receiver Carver Cheeks caught 71 passes for 926 yards and six touchdowns last season at Northern Colorado. He gives transfer quarterback EJ Colson a dangerous offensive weapon that could make some noise in the Mountain West.

The case for UTEP: As evident by the blowout spread, there isn't much of a case here. Miners coach Scotty Walden has won just five total games in his first two years at the helm and UTEP doesn't project to be better in 2026. This would be an all-time upset.

The case for OU: Think of this game like a preseason contest. Quarterback John Mateer will get a chance to show what he's improved on while coach Brent Venables' ferocious defense should feast against a lowly opponent. It'll also be a good opportunity for OU to play plenty of its backups.

articles.title: Serie A | Napoli 1-2 Como: Fabregas earns big victory at the Maradona
articles.summary: Como pounced on defensive errors to secure a big 2-1 victory away to Napoli in an early challenge for top four spots, as Martin Baturina and Tasos Douvikas w...
articles.body:
Como pounced on defensive errors to secure a big 2-1 victory away to Napoli in an early challenge for top four spots, as Martin Baturina and Tasos Douvikas were on target.

The Partenopei made two changes from the side that beat Genoa 2-0, with Matias Olivera and surprisingly Noa Lang replacing Leonardo Spinazzola and Alisson Santos, as the winger had been transfer-listed. Kevin De Bruyne was still only fit for the bench, with Alessandro Buongiorno and Luca Marianucci injured. Como opened their season with a 1-1 home draw against Udinese, again starting summer signings Trevoh Chalobah, Yan Couto, Bruno Kaiki and Luis Milla.

There was a hug before kick-off between coaches Max Allegri and Cesc Fabregas, who famously clashed on the touchline and in the press room last season.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of Napoli and Cesc Fabregas, Manager of Como interact before the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Como kept possession early doors, but Olivera pulled back from the by-line for a mad scramble in the six-yard box that Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa and Scott McTominay couldn't finish off.

Lucas Da Cunha's strike was deflected wide and Alex Valle couldn't keep the header on target from the resulting corner, but Como found the breakthrough on 16 minutes.

Assane Diao got away from Olivera down the right and rolled across for Martin Baturina, who in one sweeping movement turned around to drill into the near bottom corner from 12 yards.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Martin Baturina of Como celebrates scoring his team's first goal with teammates during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Lang really should've equalised moments later, but he turned a free header inches over from the Matteo Politano cross, then Como wasted a golden opportunity on the counter-attack with five on three, trying to walk it into the net.

That proved costly, because Napoli got the equaliser a minute later as Hojlund gathered on the edge of the area and turned to fire through a sea of legs into the bottom corner.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Rasmus Hojlund of Napoli celebrates scoring his team's first goal with coaching staff during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

However, Anguissa got into a terrible tangle playing out from the back with a poor back-pass to Amir Rrahmani, intercepted by Baturina to set up the easy Tasos Douvikas finish inside the area.

Yan Couto got back for a great tackle on Hojlund, then saw penalty appeals rejected for a nudge on Lang, but Como had two big opportunities in first half stoppages.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Martin Baturina of Como is challenged by Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa of Napoli during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

Alex Meret flew to fingertip the Baturina header over, but on the resulting corner was fortunate that the Nico Paz header squirmed under his body, getting trapped before rolling over the line.

Como continued to dominate possession and the initiative after the restart, although Olivera volleyed wide on a rare counter-attack, so Allegri introduced Kevin De Bruyne, Alisson Santos and Leonardo Spinazzola.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Scott McTominay of Napoli is challenged by Lucas Da Cunha of Como during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

This prompted a period of pressure and possession from the hosts, but Butez was quick off his line to anticipate Hojlund, then Ivan Smolcic showed brave defending to stop De Bruyne nodding in the Stanislav Lobotka cross, leading to a nasty clash of heads.

De Bruyne and Alisson Santos also had efforts inches off target, then Marc-Oliver Kempf off balance had to scramble a De Bruyne assist clear from the six-yard box. Lorenzo Lucca and Douvikas had headers straight at the respective goalkeepers in stoppages.

Lobotka did have the ball in the net at the 95th minute, but play had already been halted for Lucca's offside position in the build-up.

articles.title: Deal on! Liverpool moving forward on electric winger
articles.summary: Liverpool appear to have chosen their new winger. The Reds certainly want one and now they're moving forward on a star.Liverpool need to act fast if they're...
articles.body:
Liverpool appear to have chosen their new winger. The Reds certainly want one and now they're moving forward on a star.

Liverpool need to act fast if they're to finally find the player who replaces Mohamed Salah on the right. There are now just two days remaining in the transfer window and they're firmly up against it.

Which is insane, really. Liverpool knew Salah was leaving months before the window opened and yet they still haven't signed anyone to play on the right. That's despite the Egyptian being the only natural right-winger in the squad.

Bradley Barcola will arrive as essentially the replacement of Salah's attacking output but the player to line up on the right? That's entirely unclear and Liverpool certainly haven't signed anyone to do it.

But it at least appears that they've settled on their target with two days to go. Journalist Foday Manneh reports that Liverpool are now back in talks for Yankuba Minteh.

This is a 'reactivation' of talks for the player, with Brighton having got back to Liverpool with a price the Reds actually like. That was always the sticking point here but it seems the Seagulls are suddenly more open to a sale than they were last week.

Active talks have resumed as a result and it sounds as though Liverpool are ready to move forward on Minteh. Now, the actual price isn't mentioned so it remains to be seen if it's actually a good deal.

There's every chance that it is, though. Liverpool really have no time remaining to negotiate a full deal for a winger and anyone willing to talk is going to take precedence over the 'best' option possible.

We can only cross our collective fingers that it's an approach which at least lands Liverpool a good player. Minteh boasts the kind of potential you'd want, even if his current output is far below what you'd want.

articles.title: Justin Rose, Si Woo Kim stun fans on consecutive holes at Tour Championship
articles.summary: Justin Rose and Si Woo Kim thrilled fans at the Tour Championship with back to back shots of pure golf magic.
articles.body:
One of the quirks of the Tour Championship's limited field is that fans who settle into a single vantage point can go long stretches without seeing much action.

Those who chose to roam East Lake Golf Club on Sunday, however, were rewarded in a big way, especially anyone who latched onto the pairing of Si Woo Kim and Justin Rose.

See the best photos from the 2026 Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta

The highlight came at the par-3 ninth, where Rose pulled a 6-iron for the 208-yard shot and produced one of golf's rarest feats. His tee shot never touched the green, flying directly into the cup for a thunderous slam-dunk ace. The extraordinary hole-in-one vaulted Rose to 8 under for the championship and gave spectators a moment they won't soon forget.

For Rose, it marked the fourth ace in his PGA Tour career. Perhaps his most famous came while playing at the Rio Olympics in 2016.

Not to be outdone, on the very next hole, his playing partner Kim had 120 yards in on the 10th hole, a par-4, and pulled off another slice of magic.

articles.title: Titans to waive QB Will Levis
articles.summary: The Titans are waiving quarterback Will Levis, Paul Kuharsky of paulkuharsky.com reports.
articles.body:
The Titans are waiving quarterback Will Levis, Paul Kuharsky of paulkuharsky.com reports.

Levis' departure leaves Mitchell Trubisky and Hendon Hooker behind Cam Ward.

The Titans traded up to take the Kentucky quarterback with the first pick of the second round in 2023. The team had hoped he would succeed Ryan Tannehill, but three different head coaches didn't help his development.

He served as the Titans' starting quarterback in 2024, but Tennessee drafted Ward in 2025, and Levis spent the season on injured reserve. Levis missed all of last season after undergoing season-ending surgery on his throwing shoulder to fix the AC joint.

Levis, 27, started 21 games, going 5-16 while throwing 21 touchdowns and 16 interceptions and losing 10 fumbles.

articles.title: Patriots placing top backup swing tackle on injured reserve
articles.summary: The Patriots are reportedly placing improved second-year offensive tackle Marcus Bryant on injured reserve.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are reportedly placing second-year offensive tackle Marcus Bryant on injured reserve, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss on Sunday.

Bryant shot up the depth chart as the Patriots ' projected top swing tackle in training camp. The former seventh-round draft pick out of Missouri had worked hard to carve out a real role on the roster.

But it was ultimately halted by the injury that he sustained in the Week 2 preseason matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles .

NFL teams have two designated return spots when placing players on injured reserve. So Bryant could return after missing at least the first four games of the season. Bryant being out would now mean that rookie first-round draft pick Caleb Lomu would project as the Patriots' top backup swing tackle.

Lomu has played at both spots in training camp, but he has predominantly worked at right tackle behind veteran Morgan Moses. It has been an up-and-down summer for the former University of Utah standout, and now, he is one injury away from being thrown into the fire in his first NFL season.

Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook .

articles.title: Ben Johnson and Bears get bad news in NFL analyst's take
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears won't like this hot take on their situation.
articles.body:
Ben Johnson has already worked wonders with the Chicago Bears . There's really no reason to believe this team isn't destined for something great after rounding out the season first place in the NFC North last year.

But, it's not perfect in the Windy City. Johnson, of course, has some stuff to work out before the season really gets rolling. The sooner he does it, the better for all involved.

Josh Edwards of CBS Sports has a feature out on Thursday naming one position each NFL team should look at before the roster deadline has passed.

For Chicago, he wants to see this team work on its secondary. It makes sense, because the team's secondary has been under attack, literally, as of late, when it comes to injuries.

"The secondary has been decimated by injury this summer," he says in the piece. "Safety Coby Bryant will miss an extended period of time and Kyler Gordon, Elijah Hicks and Jaylon Jones have all been watching practice from the sideline."

He adds, "Having said all of that, head coach Ben Johnson may just decide to add another tight end."

The secondary is often a part of the lineup that gets overlooked. But, Johnson isn't the kind of guy to overlook anything. He's very calculated in how he approaches this team and its talent. Either way, don't be surprised if you see Johnson make some bold additions before the roster deadline, and one of those could be the secondary.

articles.title: NFL roster cuts: Arizona Cardinals reportedly cut CB Sean Murphy-Bunting
articles.summary: The Cardinals are cutting ties with a veteran CB with 65 career starts and $1.75 million in guaranteed salary.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals have many cuts to make before 3 p.m. Arizona time. One reported cut is a surprise.

According to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports , the Cardinals are cutting veteran cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting.

The move is surprising because has $1.75 million of his scheduled $2.39 million guaranteed. He has 65 career starts and can play both inside and outside. He worked as the Cardinals' starting nickel corner all offseason while Garrett Williams has recovered from a torn Achilles.

This move suggests that the Cardinals are confident that Williams will be able to play in Week 1, and perhaps they will keep Kalen King, who had been working as the No. 2 nickelback all offseason.

Because Murphy-Bunting is a vested veteran, he will not have to go through waivers. He might be a practice squad candidate as a result, and he will still get his guaranteed salary.

Murphy-Bunting was entering his third season with the Cardinals after signing a three-year contract in free agency. Last season, he did not play, suffering a knee injury in the offseason.

The Cardinals will announce their cuts after making the necessary moves to get to 53 players on the roster by 3 p.m. Arizona time.

articles.title: Puka Nacua, Alaric Jackson won't be placed on paid leave today
articles.summary: On Sunday, the league has placed two players on paid leave: Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper.
articles.body:
On Sunday, the league has placed two players on paid leave: Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper. Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold will join them soon.

We're told there will be no further players placed on the Commissioner Exempt list today.

This means that neither Rams receiver Puka Nacua nor Rams tackle Alaric Jackson will be placed on paid leave, at least for now.

Nacua has been sued for biting a woman on New Year's Eve. Reporting on the matter has included reference to a potential diversion program . That would trigger automatic review under the Personal Conduct Policy — and likely discipline.

Ditto for Jackson , who has previously served a two-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy. He was arrested for domestic battery, but he won't face felony charges. A diversion program is on the table in lieu of misdemeanor charges.

articles.title: Blue-chip DL raves about Florida State visit, will attend SMU game
articles.summary: 2028 four-star defensive lineman Prince Che had a great visit with Florida State this weekend, and he'll return in a week for the SMU game.
articles.body:
Four-star defensive lineman Prince Che, a 2028 recruit, made his way to Tallahassee this weekend for Florida State 's season opener against the New Mexico State Aggies. He was able to see them start the season 1-0.

It was the second game visit for Che to see FSU, as he did the same last season when they played the Miami Hurricanes. According to the 6-foot-3, 305-pounder, it was a great trip, much like his visit in March for spring practice .

He went into detail about what caught his eye the most on Saturday night.

"How the D-line came stood out. They got a lot to work with, but the pressures were there, they were pressuring the quarterback and that was really great. Overall it was great," Che said via Noles247 .

During his visit, Che chopped it up quite a bit with head coach Mike Norvell and defensive line coach Terrance Knighton. He mentioned how he liked their approach towards him.

"It was great, they were real genuine with me, they made me feel welcome. Coach Norvell, coach Knighton, I really appreciate that," Che said.

This visit won't be the only time the Seminoles see Che this season. In fact, he'll return in just over a week when they host the SMU Mustangs in their ACC opener. That is one of the biggest games of the season for Florida State, and a good performance will go a long way with Che and other top targets.

He also said FSU is one of his top schools right now. Che has offers from some of the top programs in the country like the Georgia Bulldogs , Alabama Crimson Tide , Texas Longhorns , Notre Dame Fighting Irish , Ohio State Buckeyes , Oregon Ducks , LSU Tigers , and more. So, Florida State needs to keep recruiting him heavily.

articles.title: Why Man Utd goal was allowed to stand - despite Maguire 'handball'
articles.summary: The handball law often serves to confuse supporters - and it reared its head again as Harry Maguire celebrated putting Manchester United in front against Ips...
articles.body:
The handball law often serves to confuse supporters - and it reared its head again as Harry Maguire celebrated putting Manchester United in front against Ipswich Town.

The ball came off the United defender's arm, before he then moved a few yards forward into the box and his shot found its way into the back of the net.

Surely the goal would be ruled out. After all, any handball by the scorer means the goal must be disallowed.

Apart from one very important point - Maguire did not actually score the goal.

Maguire's effort was going well wide, and deflected into the back of the net off Jacob Greaves. It was officially an own goal.

There are three exemptions for when accidental handball by the scorer does not count:

Action of a defender results in an own goal

The video assistant referee Jarred Gillett said to referee Craig Pawson: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal."

Indeed, the goal could have been disallowed had the VAR felt it was deliberate handball by Maguire.

Manchester United went on to win the game 5-2 thanks to a Bruno Fernandes hat-trick.

It is rare but we saw a similar situation in January 2023 with a goal for Brentford against Liverpool.

The ball accidentally came off the arm of Ben Mee and ended up in the back of the net, but it was not going towards goal and deflected off Ibrahima Konate for an own goal.

Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil told Sky Sports that it is "tough for a referee" to judge on what is a "complicated rule".

Former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson, speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, also had some sympathy for the officials.

"Once again we are victims of the law," said Robinson. "You can't criticise the VAR officials because they are enforcing the law that they are given.

"They train extremely hard, they learn their profession but it was a handball and Harry Maguire who struck the shot.

"Thankfully that wasn't a game-defining goal. How many times has the handball law been changed?"

Ex-Ipswich forward and Sky Sports pundit Darren Bent added: "It's one of those rules where I understand because it's there in black and white, but it still doesn't feel right.

"Harry Maguire directly impacts what happens to the ball and it ends up in the back of the net at a crucial time for Ipswich. If it hits your hand and he is the one that directly impacts it, it's not a nice one to take."

articles.title: Tennessee Titans parting ways with Will Levis
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans announced on Sunday that they are placing quarterback Will Levis on waivers as part of roster cuts.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans had a serious quarterback battle during training camp and preseason. Cam Ward is the undeniable starter, but behind him, a battle raged for who would back him up. The Titans brought in Mitch Trubisky and Hendon Hooker to compete with incumbent backup Will Levis. Today, as roster cuts are pouring in ahead of the 5:00 p.m. CST deadline to trim rosters down to 53-men, the Titans announced they are waiving Levis.

Levis was drafted by the Titans in 2023 and replaced Ryan Tannehill in Mike Vrabel's final season as head coach. Through the 2023 and 2024 seasons, Levis appeared in 21 games and completed 339 passes for 3,899 yards and 21 touchdowns. He also threw 16 interceptions and took 69 sacks, averaging a quarterback rating of 82.7.

He sat out the 2025 season after undergoing shoulder surgery during the offseason and had hopes of regaining some playing time in 2026. The Titans, though, have been open to trading Levis for a while, and since that hasn't happened, the Titans have decided to part ways with their former second-round draft pick.

With Levis on Waivers, the Titans are eating $3 million in dead cap space ($2 million in cash) if he goes unclaimed . They paid him a $906,000 bonus at the start of training camp, and his $1.1 million salary is guaranteed.

Without Levis, Trubisky and Hooker will be on the roster to back up Cam Ward in 2026.

images.caption: Tennessee Titans parting ways with Will Levis

Serie A side Fiorentina remain in the hunt to sign a new striker, having likely missed out on Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee. A deal for Everton's Beto is now slowly gathering momentum.

Get Italian Football News have looked at how La Viola did make an initial offer for the Toffees player.

Now, ViolaNews report that the Everton forward is seen as the ideal option by Fabio Grosso. Discussions between the two clubs, as a result, are progressing over a deal worth €20 million.

Beto has expressed his willingness to the move and is quite enthusiastic about the deal.

Everton's stance on this has helped Fiorentina. David Moyes' side feel Beto is up for sale and has fallen down the pecking order upfront. That is why they are closing in on Richarlison, with Thierno Barry currently the starting striker for the Scotsman.

The move would be very important for Beto, who needs to become the centre of a project once again. Fiorentina will hand him that chance, with Moise Kean on his way out. The Everton man would be a better fit than Zirkzee too, as he is a proper box presence, with the Dutchman better when dropping deeper and linking up play.

articles.title: '14,000 runs for a reason' - Root calm on form
articles.summary: Joe Root is “not too concerned” about his modest returns with the bat, saying he has “14,000 runs for a reason”.
articles.body:
Joe Root is "not too concerned" about his modest returns with the bat, saying he has "14,000 runs for a reason".

Captain Root, England's all-time leading Test run-scorer, has passed 50 only twice this summer. An average of 29.44 is his second-lowest in a home season in a 14-year international career.

The 35-year-old has been lbw nine times in his past seven Tests, including on seven occasions this summer.

But Root pointed to the challenge faced by all batters against the moving ball in the UK this summer and his own remarkable Test career. Only India great Sachin Tendulkar has more than the Yorkshireman's 14,208 runs.

"I've played this game a long time and I've always found ways of solving those problems and working it through," Root told the BBC's Today at the Test. "I don't see this as being any different.

"There's a reason why I've got 14,000 runs and a reason why I've played the best part of 15 years at this level.

"Of course it's frustrating that there's sort of a trend. There are probably four umpires' calls within that, which could have gone the other way, and the ball is probably deviating more than it ever has.

"You try and be realistic and understand where everything's at, but also be aware of what you need to do to keep improving and keep getting better. I'm pretty sure I'll get through the other side. I'm not too concerned about that."

Last summer, former Australia opener David Warner took a dig at Root's prospects of success in the Ashes series that was to follow when he said: "He will have to take the surfboard off his front leg."

At the time, Warner's suggestion Root had an lbw problem was incorrect. In a run that began in August 2022 and ended with the fourth Ashes Test in Melbourne in December, Root was lbw to seam bowlers in Test cricket on only three occasions.

However, Root's recent run of leg-before dismissals began when he was trapped by Australia's Jhye Richardson in the second innings of the Boxing Day Test. Since then he has been lbw nine times in 12 innings, all to pace bowlers.

Root's specific problem has been against right-arm bowlers, pitching the ball outside off stump and nipping it back towards him.

Of the nine dismissals in his run of lbws, none have come at the hands of bowlers with high pace, rather those with a maximum speed of around 84mph.

"You're never given anything in this game," said Root. "You have to work for everything. You have to keep working hard and I'll certainly keep doing that.

"You're constantly going to get challenged and you're constantly going to have to look to evolve and learn, but that's never been something I've shied away from and I certainly won't be doing moving forward."

Root was backed to solve the lbw issue by former England captain Michael Vaughan, who said: "He's always overcome problems and I'm pretty sure he'll overcome this one.

"It is an issue because it's happening on a regular basis but he's had issues in the past that he's managed to come back from. There's no question he'll be fine in time."

Despite no big contribution from the captain, England sealed a series win over Pakistan with a 194-run win in the second Test at Lord's.

It gave Root a second win in as many matches at the beginning of his second spell as skipper, and England their first series win since 2024.

The build-up to the second Test was dominated by the controversy surrounding England pace bowler Brydon Carse, who was dropped from the squad because of an incident outside a nightclub in Derby.

On Tuesday, Root said he was "hacked off" to be dealing with another drinking issue involving an England player and confirmed he had addressed his squad to warn them against a repeat.

On Sunday, Root said he wanted his players to celebrate the win at Lord's "sensibly".

"It's important that we're not talking about that, absolutely," said Root. "It's hard to win Test matches, it's hard to win Test series.

"Enjoy it and celebrate it, but in a sensible and grown-up way."

And Vaughan suggested the England squad should "stay in".

"Have a quiet one," he said. "I don't want to be picking up the paper tomorrow morning or mid-afternoon on social media and seeing a few clicks. You've won a good series, just have a quiet night."
authors: Stephan Shemilt - Cricket Correspondent at Lord's

images.caption: '14,000 runs for a reason' - Root calm on form
